name: Maaseiah
overview: Maaseiah was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified uniquely as the son of Ithiel. His presence is noted specifically in Nehemiah 11:7, situating him within the post-exilic community of Israel. Beyond his lineage, no additional personal details or roles are recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Maaseiah means 'YHWH is a refuge,' reflecting a trust in God's protection. This proper name, as recorded in Nehemiah 11:7, is not indicated to have been given directly by God but carries a theologically rich meaning consistent with Israelite faith.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Maaseiah was the son of Ithiel. It is inferred that he was the father of Kolaiah, establishing a direct familial line within the tribe of Benjamin. No other family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Maaseiah's significance lies in his identification among the Benjaminite inhabitants during the time of Nehemiah, highlighting the restoration and resettlement of Jerusalem after the exile. His mention as the son of Ithiel connects him to the community responsible for reestablishing Israel's presence in the land, underscoring God's faithfulness in preserving His people.
